item.title: 数千人越过摩洛哥边境，造成至少 9 人死亡，西班牙向休达部署军队
item.description:
CEUTA, Spain (AP) — Spain will deploy its military to restore order at its border withMoroccoin Ceuta after thousands ofmigrants streamed into the tiny Spanishterritory, with at least nine dying in the attempt.
The announcement came after local authorities in Ceuta had asked the central government in Madrid for reinforcements to manage a border crisis that boiled over Thursday with large crowds of people breaching the border fence.
Spain’s government said it would send the Armed Forces to help the Civil Guard “maintain security in the city of Ceuta.” It also announced that Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez would join Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska in a visit to Ceuta on Friday.
“The situation is absolute chaos,” Rachid Sbihi, head of the association that represents Spain’s Civil Guard officers who police the border in Ceuta, told The Associated Press. “It’s not possible to give precise numbers, but there are thousands of migrants crossing,” he said, adding that the border had “totally collapsed.”
Achraf Maimouni, a member of the Moroccan Association for Human Rights in northern Morocco, described the situation as “exceptional.”
“The Tarajal border was opened under unusual circumstances this morning and people crossed,” he said.
Video footage showed crowds of people, mainly Moroccans, walking around the breakwaters at Tarajal beach onto local roads. While most appeared to be young men, there were also families with women and small children.
“Viva España!” some shouted to a freelance photographer working for the AP. It was not immediately clear what prompted so many migrants to cross to Ceuta.
Spain’s government delegation in Ceuta said at least nine people died Thursday during the chaos. It did not provide details on the circumstances of the deaths but bodies could be seen floating in the water. Dozens have died this year trying to reach Ceuta, according to local authorities.
The escalation at the frontier between Spain and Morocco comes after a surge in migrants attempting to reach the small exclave, mainly by swimming, on Wednesday.
Moroccan authorities have not publicly commented on the crossings, and Morocco’s Interior Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.
Spain’s Interior Ministry said the Moroccan government was “closely cooperating” with Spain to handle the situation and that Moroccan police are stopping “numerous people” who are trying to cross the border. Both countries agreed to work together “for the return, as soon as possible, of all the people who entered Ceuta illegally.”
The ministry earlier said it would guarantee the safety of citizens and the integrity of the nation’s border but that the Spanish government could not declare a national emergency — as local authorities had asked — over migration concerns.
The chaos had ripple effects in Italy, another key destination for migrants. Premier Giorgia Meloni threatened to suspend Italy’s open-border Schengen agreement with Spain “to defend our borders and ensure the safety of our citizens,” though Italy doesn’t share a border with Spain.
Ceuta authorities had previously linked the surge to a Spanish Supreme Court ruling earlier this month that barred authorities from immediately returning migrants who arrive by sea without due process. The ruling does not apply to migrants who enter Spain by land, including by climbing over the border fence.
But some activists in Morocco expressed doubt that the ruling was behind the surge, arguing most migrants would have been unaware of such legal decisions.
Spain is a main point of arrival into Europe for migrants seeking better economic opportunities or an escape from violence in their home countries.
To reach Ceuta, located on the northern African coast, migrants often swim from the Moroccan town of Fnideq, covering about 3.1 miles (5 kilometers) to reach Spanish territory. Others attempt the crossing from the nearby town of Belyounech, where the distance is shorter.
The scenes of people streaming across the frontier recall theborder crisis of May 2021when more than 8,000 migrants poured into Ceuta in just two days.
At the time, Morocco was accused of easing border controls and allowing migrants to cross into Ceuta after Spain allowed Polisario Front leader Brahim Ghali to receive treatment at a Spanish hospital, triggering a diplomatic crisis between Rabat and Madrid. The pro-independence Polisario Front for decades has claimed to be the legitimate representative of the Sahrawi people of the Western Sahara. Morocco claims Western Sahara as its own.
Juan Jesús Vivas, the head of Ceuta’s regional government, called for the national government to declare an emergency on grounds of national security, asking for more police and for the army to be deployed on the border “to guarantee the inviolability of the frontier and citizen safety.”
He had warned Wednesday that migrant reception centers were overwhelmed with hundreds of people sleeping on the streets after more than 1,500 migrants entered the territory in the past week. Thousands more crossed overnight and on Thursday.
Spain’s Interior Ministry, which tracks irregular migration, would not confirm the number of migrants who had made it to Ceuta in the last few days but said it would publish its next migration report on Aug. 3. As of July 15, nearly 3,000 migrants had entered Ceuta by land or sea this year, according to ministry figures.
Legislation covering a declaration of national emergencies does not consider migration flows as a risk to national security, according to the ministry, which said government agencies are “coordinating to respond with speed and efficacy to the situation in Ceuta.”
Ceuta,which is perched on a historical isthmus, has been a Spanish possession since 1580. Its mixed population of Christians and Muslims, Spanish and Moroccan residents and day workers, lives in relative harmony behind a border fence that many desperate migrants from across Africa attempt to cross for a better life in Europe.
Brito reported from Barcelona, Spain. AP journalists Joseph Wilson in Barcelona and Akram Oubachir in Casablanca, Morocco, contributed to this report.

item.title: 美国和伊朗相互发射导弹，快速解决持续五个月冲突的希望渺茫
item.description:
CAIRO (AP) — The United States and Iran each fired barrages of missiles Thursday, as thepattern of back-and-forth strikestook hold again and hope dimmed for a quick end to the five-month conflict.
Followinga few days of respite, fears of a wider war have grown, with renewed fightingthreatening to engulfeven more countries. Jordan said Thursday it intercepted Iranian missiles for the second consecutive day, while Kuwait said a strike in the northern part of the country killed one person. Also this week, drones caused fires on ships at an Egyptian port, and Saudi Arabia said it came under fire from Iran-backed militias in Iraq.
The war — which in its early days President Donald Trump said would lastfour to five weeks, although he warned it could take longer — has caused the price of fuel to spike and roiled the global economy. Asmonths have passed, concerns have deepened about using up thestockpile of weaponsthe U.S. needs to defend its bases and allies.
The war is unpopular among Americans, and anew AP-NORC pollsays Trump’s approval rating on Iran has dipped slightlysince last month.
The recent pause in fighting, which began over the weekend and spurred hopes among mediators of diplomatic progress, ended with increasing missile and drone attacks across many countries in the Middle East.
“We note with concern that the security situation remains precarious,” said Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesperson Tahir Andrabi, whose country has been a key mediator.
Talks “are ongoing to normalize the situation, particularly the situation in the Strait of Hormuz,” he told reporters.
An Iranian strike hit a Chinese firm’s building in Kuwait on Thursday, severely damaging the structure and killing a worker, Kuwait’s military said, hours after Jordan’s air defenses shot down five missiles launched from Iran.
No injuries were reported from Jordan’s interception, the country’s state-run Petra news agency said, quoting the spokesman for the country’s armed forces. Both Jordan and Kuwait host American troops.
The attacks came after the U.S. military saidit completed “a heavy wave of strikes against Iran”in response to an earlier Iranian missile attack on a U.S. base in Jordan.
U.S. Central Command said U.S. forces struck dozens of targets belonging to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, and coastal surveillance and defense sites.
Iran’s official IRNA news agency said three people were killed and two were wounded in a strike on the island of Qeshm, which lies off the Iranian mainland in the Strait of Hormuz — a crucial waterway for the world’s energy supplies that has been at the center of the conflict.
The latest barrage came after the U.S. partnered with Saudi Arabia on Wednesday to strike Iran-backed militias in Iraq, killing at least 20 fighters and six Iranian advisers.
Also on Wednesday, British maritime security firm Ambrey said drone strikes ignited fires on two natural gas vessels at the Egyptian port of Damietta. It was not immediately clear who was responsible for the strikes on a U.S.-owned floating storage facility and a Greek-owned tanker. No injuries were reported.
The office of the Egyptian prime minister said initial investigations showed the fires had been caused by a drone. In a cabinet meeting, Prime Minister Mustafa Madbouly said investigators were able to recover traces of the drone and will try to determine where it came from.
Egypt, a close U.S. ally and regional mediator, has until now been spared direct military action during the war. A strike by Iran or its allies, if confirmed, would mark a significant widening of the conflict. The Iran-backedHouthi rebels in Yemenhave denied they were behind the attack.
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi didn’t outright deny Iranian involvement but said: “Egypt is an important friend and partner in the region, and its security is of utmost importance to us.”
“We must all be vigilant against Israeli plots and false-flag operations designed to undermine regional peace,” he said on X. “The threat is clear, mutual, and fearful of Muslim solidarity.”
The conflict has wreaked havoc on the global economy as energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have ground to a near halt. Much of the diplomacy around ending the war has focused on reopening the strait, through which 20% of oil and natural gas shipments passed in peacetime.
The already limited traffic through the strait has plunged to wartime lows during the recent exchange of strikes, from 82 ships during the week of July 13-19 to just 39 from July 20-26, Lloyd’s List Intelligence, a shipping data and analysis firm, said in an webinar.
Fighting elsewhere has squeezed energy supplies further.
Saudi Arabia has accused Iraqi militias of firing drones against its oil facilities over the past days. An umbrella group of Iraqi militias initially denied the allegations, while the Houthi rebels said they had attacked Saudi energy facilities as part of aseparate but related conflict.
The Houthis have also declared a blockade of Saudi shipping andthreatened to choke offanother crucial Middle East trade route, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from the Red Sea into the Gulf of Aden. That route became even more important during the war, as Saudi Arabia used it tobypass the Strait of Hormuz.
While some Saudi oil exports are continuing through the Bab al-Mandab Strait despite the blockade, Lloyd’s List Intelligence said much of that oil now follows an expensive and time-consuming workaround: It travels from Saudi Arabia on tankers to the Egyptian city of Ain Sokhna on the Red Sea coast before being pumped overland through a pipeline to the Mediterranean port of Sidi Kerir. Then it’s loaded on tankers again.
The Suez Canal is not deep enough to handle the largest and most economical tankers when they are fully loaded with oil.
Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman met Wednesday with Trump and Vice President JD Vance, according to two people familiar with the matter who were not authorized to comment publicly about the private meetings.
They said the Saudi decision to join the U.S. attacks against the Iraqi militias was meant to send a message to Iran that the kingdom would not tolerate Iran or its proxies targeting the Saudi oil industry and other critical infrastructure. At the same time, the defense minister underscored to Trump and Vance that the Saudis want to see a de-escalation in the war and for Washington and Tehran to return to negotiations.
Becatoros reported from Athens, Greece. Associated Press writers Konstantin Toropin and Aamer Madhani in Washington; Qassim Abdul-Zahra in Baghdad; Fatma Khaled in Cairo; and Christopher Weber in Los Angeles contributed.

item.title: 随着来自摩洛哥的移民数量激增，关于西班牙飞地休达需要了解什么
item.description:
马德里（美联社）——数千名移民从摩洛哥涌入西班牙位于北非的休达领地，至少有 18 人在尝试中死亡，促使西班牙部署军队恢复边境。
来自边境的视频和图像显示，一大群人，主要是摩洛哥人，在摩洛哥边境检查站附近的城市海滩的防波堤上行走，走上当地道路。大多数看起来是年轻男性，但也有一些有妇女和儿童的家庭。
前一天，试图通过游泳方式抵达这片飞地的移民激增，导致边境局势升级。目前尚不清楚是什么促使这么多人越境前往休达。
西班牙政府表示将派遣武装部队帮助休达的国民警卫队，西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯预计将于周五访问休达。
休达和东边约 400 公里（250 英里）的更大的西班牙领土梅利利亚位于非洲尖端的地中海沿岸北岸。这两个自治城市都属于西班牙，并与非洲共享欧盟唯一的陆地边界。
自 1580 年起，休达就被西班牙占领，这里是基督徒和穆斯林混杂人口的家园，西班牙人和摩洛哥居民以及日工的生活相对和谐。
摩洛哥并未正式承认休达和梅利利亚为西班牙领土，并经常将其称为被占领土地。
在最近的记忆中，这座拥有 85,000 人口的城市一直是马德里和拉巴特之间重大外交危机的爆发点。
2021年5月，摩洛哥政府取消边境管制，短短两天内就让来自摩洛哥和撒哈拉以南国家的约8000人涌入休达。
此举被广泛解读为摩洛哥对西班牙决定允许来自有争议的西撒哈拉地区的支持独立领导人在西班牙医院接受治疗的报复。
直到西班牙首相改变了该国在西撒哈拉问题上的长期立场，并于次年会见摩洛哥国王穆罕默德六世后，紧张局势才得以缓和，边界也得以恢复。
西班牙是寻求更好经济机会或逃离祖国暴力的移民进入欧洲的主要目的地。
休达及其姊妹城市梅利利亚戒备森严，因为这些领土被视为那些试图从摩洛哥和非洲其他地区前往西班牙的人的目的地。
许多到达休达或梅利利亚的移民立即被遣返，而其他被关押在移民庇护所的移民则得到处理，可以在西班牙申请庇护。
为了到达休达，移民经常从摩洛哥小镇费尼迪克游泳，游大约 5 公里（3.1 英里）到达西班牙领土。其他人则尝试从附近的贝柳内奇镇穿越，那里的距离较短。
尽管如此，到达休达和梅利利亚的移民人数总体上远低于通过加那利群岛和巴利阿里群岛到达西班牙的移民人数。
近几十年来，西班牙的总体移民人口大幅增长，在这个拥有 5000 万人口的国家中，约有 1000 万人出生在其他地方。
许多人来自哥伦比亚、委内瑞拉和摩洛哥，在西班牙经济的关键部门工作，包括农业、旅游业和服务业。

item.title: 在五角大楼的压力下，美国童子军放弃了活动中的多样性倡议
item.description:
达拉斯（美联社）——美国童子军最大的集会之一取消了为同性恋青年、女性和有色人种童子军提供的专用空间，因为该组织面临五角大楼要求撤回多元化努力的压力。
周五结束的全国童军大会的变化反映了自美国童子军组织成为国防部长皮特·赫格斯索（Pete Hegsetheth）所谓的“觉醒”政策的目标以来该组织所做的转变。一些原计划参加在西弗吉尼亚州举行的活动的童子军表示，他们退出了，因为美国童子军取消了之前庆祝的包容性举措。
赫格斯威胁说，如果美国童子军不做出改变，包括重新关注多元化倡议，它将结束五角大楼与美国童子军长达百年的合作关系。该组织以前称为美国童子军，于 2024 年重新命名，以强调包容性和童子军队伍中女孩数量的不断增加。
“童军从根本上来说是年轻人享受乐趣的安全场所，”曾在之前的全国赛事中组织过包容性活动的助理童子军队长塞缪尔·J·阿伦森 (Samuel J. Aronson) 说。“如果没有这些空间，我们就剥夺了成千上万年轻人的安全和乐趣。”
今年，来自全国各地的约 15,000 名童军、领袖和志愿者将参加在西弗吉尼亚州山区举行的为期 10 天的活动。除了山地自行车和皮划艇等活动外，聚会还举办领导力项目和教育课程。
美国童子军发言人表示，该组织仍然“完全致力于欢迎和服务所有青少年”，但没有回答有关狂欢活动变化的问题。
五角大楼在二月份与美国童子军组织达成了一项协议，但双方对该协议的描述相互矛盾。本月，一名同性恋权利活动人士在提起诉讼后从国防部获得了概述该协议的备忘录，他认为明确性对公众很重要。
这份六页的文件详细说明了五角大楼监控合规性的方式，包括每个组织的官员将根据需要“定期接触点和会面”。它是由詹姆斯·戴尔 (James Dale) 获得的，他在 20 世纪 90 年代初因同性恋而被童子军开除，后来因歧视而被起诉。他将五角大楼的策略等同于恶霸的行为。
“他们基本上对组织有控制权，在持续的压力下威胁他们，”戴尔说。
侦察兵和军队长期以来一直保持着密切的联系。军方为狂欢活动提供后勤支持，一些侦察部队在基地或附近集结。
当被问及该交易的实施和监督时，五角大楼发言人提到了赫格斯之前的评论。
今年 2 月，赫格斯发布了一段视频，称他的部门将“大力审查”美国童子军所做的改变，如果该组织未能在 8 月下旬遵守规定，将停止军方对该组织的长期支持。
约翰·安德鲁·塞格巴特 (John Andrew Segebarth) 是一名 21 岁的大学生，也是鹰级童子军 (Eagle Scout)，他对该协议感到沮丧。他在一年级时就加入了童子军行列，并表示他一直期待在今年的狂欢节上为 LGBTQ+ 和联盟童子军配备人员。
塞格巴特是一名同性恋，并在 2024 年被同行选举为国家童子军官员，他表示，取消包容性空间对于美国童子军来说是一个巨大的逆转。阿伦森表示，近年来的全国童子军活动包括女童子军、有色人种童子军、LGBTQ+童子军和残疾人的社区空间。
“童军运动有点背离了他们告诉我他们所相信的价值观，”塞格巴斯说，他和阿伦森一起决定不参加今年的狂欢活动。
正是在一个社区帐篷里，蕾拉·格蕾丝找到了第一个可以公开谈论自己是跨性别女性的地方。格蕾丝现年 21 岁，是一名助理童子军队长，她还计划今年为西弗吉尼亚州的 LGBTQ+ 和联盟童子军配备人员。
当空间被取消时，格蕾丝说她几乎没有去参加聚会，但她决定去那里帮助那些有需要的人。她最终在一个致力于解决心理健康、粮食安全和教育等问题的领域担任志愿者。
她正试图填补因取消包容性区域而留下的空白。
“我身上有很多彩虹，我的右手指甲上画着女同性恋旗帜，我的左手指甲上画着变性人旗帜，”她说。“我正在尽我最大的努力，希望能够弥补社区空间的不足。”
美联社记者本·芬利在华盛顿对这篇报道做出了贡献。

item.title: 警方描述了一位父亲在意识到当时的妻子林赛·克兰西杀死了他们的 3 个孩子后的恐惧
item.description:
马萨诸塞州普利茅斯（美联社）——两名警察首先关注的是林赛·克兰西（Lindsay Clancy）从马萨诸塞州家中二楼窗户跳下后，在雪地里时而昏迷时而昏迷不醒的情景。几分钟之内，她当时的丈夫尖叫着说他们的三个孩子都死了，他们就冲进了地下室。
“我不能叫醒他们——我不能让他们起来！”他疯狂地告诉警察，他们与消防员和护理人员一起在周四向陪审员提供了第一手的事故后果。
谋杀案审判的重点是克兰西当时的精神状态。她的律师并不否认她用健身带勒死了孩子们。但他们说她患有产后精神病，这是一种罕见的精神疾病，与分娩后的压力、睡眠不足和荷尔蒙变化有关。
检察官称，克兰西是马萨诸塞州总医院的前分娩护士，他对 2023 年 1 月的死亡事件负有故意和刑事责任。
编者注：如果您或您认识的人需要帮助，可以通过拨打或发短信 988 联系美国的全国自杀和危机生命热线。也可以通过 988lifeline.org 进行在线聊天
陪审员们花了两天时间听取了帕特里克·克兰西的证词和他痛苦的 911 电话，随后做出了这份证词。当他还在打电话时，他发现了 3 岁的道森、5 岁的科拉和 8 个月大的卡兰的尸体，几分钟后，他从妻子让他跑的差事回到家。
帕特里克·克兰西在接受采访时表示，他原谅了他的前妻，他认为她是病态的而不是邪恶的。这次审判标志着他自杀人事件以来第一次见到林赛·克兰西。
当晚，她用多种方法试图结束自己的生命，但腰部以下仍处于瘫痪状态。据她的律师说，有一个声音告诉她：“这是你最后的机会。杀死孩子们，这样你就可以自杀了。”
警官斯蒂芬·霍尔和布莱恩·约瑟芬周四作证说，他们分别被派往波士顿南部沿海小镇达克斯伯里的房子。霍尔说，他们到达时发现帕特里克·克兰西在屋后大喊救命。
帕特里克·克兰西本周早些时候作证说，他受伤的妻子告诉他孩子们在地下室，但她没有说他们已经死了。
约瑟芬作证说，当警察沿着他的尖叫声下楼时，只有 8 个月大的卡兰有微弱的脉搏。
“根据我之前发生的事件的训练经验，我知道这不会有什么好处，”约瑟芬说。他们开始在消防员的帮助下提供援助。
消防部门主管 PJ Hussey 及时赶到，透过地下室的窗户看到帕特里克·克兰西解开孩子脖子上的健身带。
赫西作证说，随着更多的救护车赶到房子，“事情很快就变得非常混乱”。达克斯伯里消防员兼护理人员詹妮弗·斯特拉顿表示，婴儿再也没有恢复脉搏。
如果谋杀罪名成立，林赛·克兰西将面临终身监禁且不得假释。如果因缺乏刑事责任而被判无罪，她将被送往州立精神卫生机构。
在周一的开庭辩论中，她的律师表示，她患有双相情感障碍，在她第三个孩子出生后服用的抗抑郁药物使她的病情恶化。
帕特里克·克兰西作证称，在凶杀案发生前的几个月里，他妻子的心理健康状况不断恶化。他说她告诉他有关伤害孩子的侵入性想法以及自杀的想法。
她向产后情绪障碍专家寻求治疗，并接受了多种精神药物治疗。没有任何效果后，她住进了精神病院。她在出院19天后杀害了孩子们。
根据今年早些时候提起的诉讼，克兰西和她的前夫指责她的医疗服务提供者未能正确诊断、治疗和监测她。

item.title: 西雅图警察局长因应对节日枪击事件而在市长压力下辞职
item.description:
西雅图（美联社）——西雅图警察局长周四辞职，原因是该市在上周末美食节上发生致命枪战的关键信息发布缓慢。
在市长凯蒂·威尔逊宣布这一消息之前，人们对警察局长肖恩·巴恩斯是否会辞职进行了数小时的猜测，因为他的一些支持者表示，他拒绝了威尔逊的辞职请求。
威尔逊表示，她任命副局长安德烈·赛尔斯（Andre Sayles）为临时局长，他是一位拥有二十多年经验的执法老手。
巴恩斯周四早些时候告诉《西雅图时报》，他是否继续担任市长“取决于市长”。他说他今天休假并与家人共度时光。
市长在一份书面声明中表示，她对巴恩斯的服务表示感谢。声明中巴恩斯表示很荣幸能够为这座城市服务。
巴恩斯说：“我希望这一转变让这座城市和这个部门有机会重新集中精力关注最重要的事情，解决青少年枪支暴力问题并防止更多悲剧发生。”
上周末，西雅图之咬节（Bite of Seattle）爆发枪声，巴恩斯当时正在城外参加执法会议。西雅图咬节节是一年一度的为期三天的节日，吸引了数百名食品和零售摊贩及表演者。包括一名嫌疑人在内的三人死亡，四人受伤。其中一名受伤者是一名2岁男孩。
法庭文件显示，现场有数十名警察，其中至少一名警察看到一名 15 岁嫌疑人向人群开枪，并迅速劝说他投降。警方仍在寻找至少另一人。
虽然威尔逊认为警方的快速反应可能挽救了生命，但她也承认，事后该市的沟通速度很慢。
在社交媒体最初发布枪击事件消息后，警方花了近五个小时才向公众提供更多信息，包括是否存在任何持续的威胁。该市也未能通过紧急警报系统发出任何通知。与此同时，威尔逊宣布有两人被拘留，但她后来撤回了这一声明。
西雅图警察局助理局长 Tyrone Davis 终于在晚上 11 点左右提供了最新情况。周日举行的新闻发布会上，市长、州长鲍勃·弗格森和美国众议员普拉米拉·贾亚帕尔也出席了会议。
威尔逊在周四的视频声明中表示：“当时我没有完全理解，自事件下午 6 点发生以来，公众或媒体获得的信息是多么的少。”“如果我知道这一点，我会敦促立即通报情况，而不是等待组织新闻发布会。”
巴恩斯是西雅图第二位黑人警察局长。
包括西雅图全国有色人种协进会和西雅图大都会城市联盟在内的几个黑人社区组织周四集会，试图挽救他的工作。在给市长办公室的一封公开信中，他们称赞他改善了该部门与社区之间的关系，帮助减少了枪支暴力并加强了该部门的运作。
信中说：“巴恩斯局长不应成为公共安全复杂挑战的替罪羊。”
至少六名市议会成员发表声明支持巴恩斯。一份由四人签署的声明指出，该市在不到三年的时间内更换了四位酋长。
“我们的首要任务必须是稳定，而不是进一步的破坏，”它说。
巴恩斯在担任威斯康星州麦迪逊市警察局局长后，于 2024 年 12 月被西雅图前市长布鲁斯·哈雷尔任命。
当威尔逊——一位曾经支持取消警察经费的民主社会主义者——去年赢得市长竞选时，她让巴恩斯继续担任市长。这向该市的商业机构和社区团体发出了一个信号，即她不打算对公共安全采取截然不同的做法。
西雅图市中心协会主席乔恩·斯科尔斯(Jon Scholes)在一份电子邮件声明中表示，“西雅图在公共安全方面一直在积极发展，警察招聘呈上升趋势，犯罪率呈下降趋势。”“下一任警察局长必须能够保持已经取得的进展，并为我们的社区注入信心。”
巴恩斯因在家人居住的芝加哥度过时光而受到一些批评。中士。该部门发言人帕特里克·米肖(Patrick Michaud)周四表示，巴恩斯今年已四次前往芝加哥，总共花了大约18天的时间。
辞职之际，西雅图即将迎来另一个大型节日周末。2026 年 Seafair 周末节——划船活动、航空表演和节日——将于周五开始。

item.title: 美联社-NORC 的一项新民意调查显示，人们对特朗普处理伊朗问题的看法发生了怎样的转变
item.description:
▶ Follow today’slive updates on the Trump administration
WASHINGTON (AP) — Most Americans saythe war in Iranhas not been worth fighting, and President Donald Trump’s approval rating on Iran has fallen slightlysince last month, according to a new AP-NORC poll.
The results are a stark repudiation of the Republican president’s approach to the conflict, which has dragged on far longer than he originally predicted.
About two-thirds of U.S. adults say the war with Iran, whichbegan Feb. 28, has not been worthwhile, according to the new poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research. That includes the vast majority of Democrats and independents, as well as about 37% of Republicans.
The poll was conducted July 23-27, as the U.S. and Iran paused attacks following anearly two-week escalationin the war. During the escalation, the U.S. targeted Iranian military and commercial sites while Iran attacked U.S. military facilities in the Middle East, resulting inadditional deaths of American service members. Since the war began, 18 U.S. service members have been killed, butthe Trump administration has sought to revisethose numbers.
The survey reinforces how unpopular the Iran war has become at home, a potential problem forcongressional Republicans up for reelection in November who have defendedTrump’s military actions. Just 28% of U.S. adults now approve of how Trump is handling Iran, a slight decline from 34% last month. Even Republicans appear to be increasingly unhappy with the prolonged conflict. Roughly 61% of Republicans approve of how Trump is handling Iran, an apparent decline from 71% in June. The margin of sampling error for Republicans is 6 points, so the decline is considered slight, but it’s still noteworthy given Republicans’ much higher approval of how Trump is handling the presidency overall.
Trump’s overall approval rating is at 33%, slightly below where he stood at this point in his first term and similar to where former President Joe Biden stood about one and a half years into his presidency, when inflation peaked.
Robert McClary, a 52-year-old Republican from Sugar Grove, Ohio, is skeptical the war could be brought to an easy conclusion and disapproves of Trump’s handling of it. McClary voted for the president once, in 2016, but recalls that during the last election, Trump campaigned onnot starting new wars in the Middle East.
“I don’t have any trust in this administration at all and to why they brought us into this war, why they’re putting our soldiers at risk again,” he said.
The findings also indicate that most Americans’ goals for the conflict may not be aligned with Trump, who has repeatedly said the war was launched tokeep a nuclear weapon out of Iran’s hands. While about two-thirds of U.S. adults say it’s “extremely” or “very” important to keep Iran from gaining a nuclear weapon — with Republicans especially likely to say this — even more Americans say it’s highly important for the U.S. to keep gasoline prices low or negotiate a permanent ceasefire with Iran.
McClary added: “I really don’t know what you can do now. I mean, you’ve kind of gotten yourself buried into this mess.”
There’s little appetite among Americans for a prolonged conflict.
Only about 2 in 10 U.S. adults want to continue military action in Iran, while about 3 in 10 say the U.S. should pause military action and seek a renewed ceasefire through negotiations. About 2 in 10 want to completely stop military action in Iran and roughly one-quarter don’t know enough to say.
About half of Republicans say the U.S. should continue military action against Iran, particularly those who identify as “very conservative.” Republicans who identify as MAGA — part of Trump’s Make America Great Again movement — are much likelier than non-MAGA Republicans to say the war should continue. Non-MAGA Republicans are more likely to want a ceasefire or a complete halt to the military action.
Jennifer Norton, a 71-year-old Republican from Crossville, Tennessee, supports military action in Iran but has been displeased to see prices rising for things like beef roasts and hamburgers. Norton lives on a “modest income,” and things are getting expensive.
“I am getting a little impatient, but when I start to dwell on that for a minute, I remember Mr. President Trump is a brilliant businessman,” she said. “He can’t tell us exactly what he’s doing, but I trust that he’s doing something. I mean, he is doing fine.”
Independents and Democrats are more likely than Republicans to want to stop military action against Iran immediately, although about 3 in 10 Republicans want either a pause or complete stop to military action.
Ryan Sloan, a 39-year-old Republican in Lakeland, Florida, has come to disapprove of the conflict in Iran recently because he wants a better explanation from the Trump administration about why the war intensified in late July.
“Let’s face it, not everybody’s going to be happy with him,” Sloan said. “I just wish I’d have had more transparency about why things were going on the way they were.”
Many Americans continue to be concerned about the pocketbook impact of the Iran war. About 7 in 10 U.S. adults — 72% — say it’s “extremely” or “very” important for the U.S. to prevent domestic oil and gas prices from rising, up slightly from 67% in March.
Oiltopped $100 a barrel last week, ending a brief period of lower prices when hostilities between the U.S. and Iran eased in June. Gas prices rose above $4 per gallon on average, and the elevated fuel price is hitting consumers in other ways, too. Inflation cooled last month but remains elevated, and consumer spendinghas slowed, with signs that Americans are taking advantage of sales and other incentives.
There are also indications that fluctuating gasoline prices are an increasingly big problem for many Americans. About 4 in 10 say the cost of gas for their car is a “major source” of stress in their life right now, compared with about 3 in 10 in February.
Mikal Baker, a 47-year-old political independent in Sandy Springs, Georgia, disapproves of the war in Iran and is frustrated by the effect on gas prices.
“I don’t see the benefit. I don’t see the total benefit of the American citizen for this war,” he said. But Baker is skeptical it will ever come to an end. “I can’t say it will ever be over with.”
Some Americans may be hoping that gasoline prices could stabilize or go down. About 4 in 10 U.S. adults are “extremely” or “very” concerned about being able to afford gas in the next few months, down slightly from 45% in March.
Even as most Americans prioritize keeping gas prices from rising, a similar share say it’s “extremely” or “very” important to negotiate a permanent ceasefire with Iran.
About 7 in 10 Americans say it’s “extremely” or “very” important for the U.S. to reach a ceasefire agreement, slightly higher than the roughly two-thirds who say it’s at least “very” important to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. That’s also well above the 4 in 10 who say it’s “extremely” or “very” important to prevent Iran from threatening Israel.
Early in the conflict, Trump saidthe United States’ primary objectiveswere to degrade Iran’s military capability, eliminate their Navy and Air Force, keep them from gaining nuclear weapons and protect U.S. allies in the region.
Republicans, in particular, say it’s highly important to keep Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. About 8 in 10 say this is at least “very” important, compared with roughly 7 in 10 who say that about preventing oil and gas prices from rising and negotiating a permanent ceasefire with Iran.
Sloan, the Florida Republican, believes it’s important to keep Iran from gaining a nuclear weapon, adding: “We are most definitely their number one targets once they do have nuclear capabilities.”
The AP-NORC poll of 1,165 adults was conducted July 23-27 using a sample drawn from NORC’s probability-based AmeriSpeak Panel, which is designed to be representative of the U.S. population. The margin of sampling error for adults overall is plus or minus 3.7 percentage points. The margin of sampling error is plus or minus 6.0 for Republicans overall and plus or minus 5.4 for Democrats overall.

item.title: 特朗普品牌纪念护照将在美国各地发售
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——美国国务院周四表示，首都以外的美国人很快就能获得印有唐纳德·特朗普总统照片的限量版美国护照，庆祝美国250岁生日。
该部门在全国范围内的 27 家护照代理机构将于下个月开始提供特殊旅行证件。此前，这些服务只能在华盛顿特区的护照办公室向亲自申请的申请人提供。
特朗普的严肃肖像印在内页上，他是旅行证件中第一位出现在世的总统。
这些护照是特朗普将自己的名字和肖像添加到建筑物、文件和其他引人注目的纪念物中的最新例子。美国造币厂已开始生产以金制成的纪念建国纪念币，上面印有他的头像，并且正在努力将特朗普的签名印在所有新的美国纸币上，这对于在任总统来说也是第一次。
“为了满足巨大的需求，国务院正在向公众额外提供 25 万份特别纪念护照，”它在一份声明中表示。“全国各地的美国人现在将有机会申请其中一种额外的特殊护照，即‘爱国者护照’。”
科罗拉多州 Centennial 的护照办事处；芝加哥；达拉斯；底特律;新奥尔良；纽约;康涅狄格州斯坦福将从 8 月 8 日开始在为期一天的特别活动中提供特朗普护照。整个 8 月份，该名单将包括其他护照办事处。
想要特殊护照的人必须在该部门护照网站上指定的日期亲自申请。想要传统护照的人必须在不同的日子申请。
纪念护照在内页上印有特朗普的照片，并在他的金色签名上印有特朗普的照片，而封面的顶部有粗体金色印刷的“美利坚合众国”字样，底部有“护照”字样——这与当前标准封面相反。
此外，后盖底部还有一面小型金色层压美国国旗，上面有星星环绕的数字 250。
目前美国护照上唯一出现的总统是南达科他州拉什莫尔山的双页描绘——乔治·华盛顿、托马斯·杰斐逊、西奥多·罗斯福和亚伯拉罕·林肯。
其他描绘包括自由女神像、费城的自由钟和独立厅，以及大平原、山脉和岛屿的场景。目前的护照还包含马丁·路德·金以及华盛顿、杰斐逊、罗斯福、约翰·F·肯尼迪和德怀特·艾森豪威尔总统的名言。
将特朗普的照片和签名添加到护照簿上是他的助手为提高总统知名度而采取的最新举措，包括将他的名字添加到美国和平建设研究所和肯尼迪中心表演艺术场所，尽管该标牌后来根据法院命令被删除。
特朗普还计划在弗吉尼亚州通往华盛顿的一个入口处建造一座新的白宫宴会厅和一座巨大的拱门，这也引起了轰动。

item.title: 反对派蔓延，欧洲国家誓言抵制因凡蒂诺私募股权计划
item.description:
GENEVA (AP) — European nations agreed Thursday to boycott the World Cup and all other FIFA competitions to protest Gianni Infantino’s plan tosell stakes in soccer’s biggest tournamentto private equity investors. The North American soccer body rejected his plan later the same day.
“UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions,” the European soccer body said after an urgent online meeting of its 55 member nations.
FIFA issued a statement early Friday saying that “nobody is selling football” and that it plans to continue the consultation process. But it appeared to back off from establishing the public equity move — what it calls the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) — if member countries do not agree.
“FIFA acknowledges and respects feedback and concern aired in public,” it said, while blaming “erroneous reporting in the media” for disruptions to its planned consultation with member associations.
But it said that without the support of FIFA’s 211 member associations, “FIFA’s commercial activities would remain unchanged. FFE would not be established.”
“Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.”
The next scheduled FIFA tournament is within weeks in Europe — the Women’s Under-20 World Cup hosted by Poland from Sept. 5 — and the four British federations comprise FIFA’s only bidder to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup. That decision is due Nov. 23.
“Some things are simply too important to sell,” UEFA said in a statement. “The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”
The strategy meeting was called to counter FIFA PresidentInfantino’s offer of $20 millionto each of FIFA’s 211 global members that has to be accepted by mid-September.
Later Thursday, the 41-member Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) met and announced it rejected Infantino’s plan.
In a statement, CONCACAF said members “expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies.” It also questioned the need for outside investment “following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history.”
Infantino’s secret project was revealed Tuesday to spin off its commercial operations in the new $20 billion FFE subsidiary 20% owned by private investors. The core investor would be a New York investment firm created by Joshua Kushner, the brother of U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.
Infantino wrote Tuesday to the 211 members — already the effective owners of FIFA as a non-profit association under Swiss law — that if they approve FFE their promised $10 million basic funding for the next four years will double to $20 million. He projected their FIFA funding through 2038 would be $86 million each, instead of about $36 million.
“This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football,” said UEFA, where Infantino was a long-time staffer and its CEO-like general secretary when he was first elected to lead FIFA in 2016.
Infantino’s high-stakes financial gambit now could threaten his previously secure 11-year presidency of FIFA as anger and frustration with him rises among soccer stakeholders including three of the six continental bodies.
FIFA has set a Nov. 18 deadline for potential candidates to declare in a presidential vote of the 211 members scheduled next March in Rabat, Morocco.
Infantino had seemed — 11 days ago after the World Cup final in East Rutherford, New Jersey — to have a clear path to being re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term in office through 2031, despite afuror over letting United States forward Folarin Balogun playagainst Belgium despite a red card in his previous game.
Soccer officials have said privately Infantino has eyed a lucrative commissioner-like role at the FFE spinoff beyond 2031.
“Game over, Gianni #InfantinOUT,” the Football Supporters Europe group, which advises UEFA on fan issues such as ticket prices, posted after the boycott threat.
UEFA detailed Thursday why soccer officials fear external investors owning a stake of the global game’s biggest events, including World Cups and Club World Cups for men and women.
“The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever,” UEFA said. “Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure.”
Infantino has presented the private equity offer as a chance to “turbocharge” funding development of soccer across the world, where a majority of the 211 FIFA members rely on its funding.
Officials from about 40 UEFA member spoke at the urgent meeting, with anger expressed that FIFA is not using some of its multi-billion reserves to fund extra development programs.
“As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive,” the European soccer body said, “unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.”
On a seismic day in soccer politics, a traditional bedrock of support in Asia for FIFA and Infantino had earlier Thursday been shaken.
“FIFA’s unilateral actions appear to undermine the very foundations of continental football,” the Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said in a letter to its 46 members of FIFA, warning of risks to their own competitions.
Sheikh Salman, an ally to Infantino since losing theFIFA presidential election to him in 2016, wrote “such an initiative will not succeed without the support of all the confederations, which is not the case now.”
In a video message published Wednesday by FIFA, Infantino insisted spinning off its money-making operations was “an offer, not an obligation.”
A FIFA presentation for its members, co-written with its banking advisors from J.P. Morgan and seen by the AP, set a goal for FFE as “commercial rigor and expertise to better capitalize on broadcast rights, sponsorships and a growing tournament portfolio.”
That growing portfolio likely would include adding more teams to FIFA competitions like the World Cup and Club World Cup for men and women, and potentially staging them more often than every four years, including in the U.S.
FIFA adding teams, games and competitions would squeeze the value, status and space in thecongested global fixture calendarfor those that fund and are organized by the six continental soccer bodies like UEFA and the AFC. Those include World Cup qualifying games, continental tournaments and Champions Leagues.
“It is important that the AFC family has a complete understanding,” Sheikh Salman wrote, “of how such an initiative may affect key areas of global and Asian football, including the sustainability of confederation and (domestic) competitions, as well as the organization and commercial landscape surrounding the AFC’s activities.”
A threatenedWorld Cup boycott from Europehelped derail Infantino’s plan in 2021 to play World Cups every two years instead of four.

item.title: 警方称，前牛仔四分卫托尼·罗莫被捕时车内有一瓶打开的酒
item.description:
密尔沃基（美联社）——当局称，哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）美国国家橄榄球联盟（NFL）分析师、前达拉斯牛仔队四分卫托尼·罗莫（Tony Romo）上周被警方拦下时，车内装有一个开着的酒精容器，后来因涉嫌酒后驾车而被捕。
根据密尔沃基县治安官办公室发布的三份传票之一，在罗莫黑色吉普车被拖走之前的盘点过程中，在乘客侧发现了“一瓶打开的酒精饮料”。
另一份传票称，7月23日，警方在43号州际公路上拦截了罗莫，因为有人看到他在一个戈尔区超车，该戈尔区将州际交通与从入口匝道进入的车辆分开。警方表示，罗莫在拦截过程中询问了什么是血腥区域。
罗莫在现场清醒测试中表现不佳，被拘留、登记并释放。法庭记录显示，罗莫后来因拒绝“被捕后接受醉酒测试”而被传唤。他定于 9 月 21 日出庭。
根据本周早些时候发布的随身摄像机镜头，罗莫告诉警员，他当时是从高尔夫球场出来的，正准备“去看望爷爷奶奶”，但被拦住了。
一名副警长告诉罗莫，他怀疑罗莫身体有问题，因为他有“玻璃般的红色眼睛”和“令人陶醉的酒精饮料的气味”。
罗莫在距离威斯康星州伯灵顿密尔沃基约 35 英里的高中上学。
46 岁的罗莫自 2017 年以来一直担任哥伦比亚广播公司 NFL 报道的首席比赛分析师，他在 2004-16 赛季的 NFL 职业生涯中四次参加职业碗比赛，并且完全在达拉斯度过。
罗莫以 248 次达阵传球，仍然是牛仔队队内的领军人物。他一直保持着队史职业传球码数纪录（34,183 码），直到上赛季达克·普雷斯科特超越他。

item.title: WNBA 表示，社交媒体帖子显示布克斯和里斯对比赛的投注“没有达到目标”
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——WNBA 周四表示，一篇社交媒体帖子显示，明星佩奇·比克斯 (Paige Bueckers) 和安吉尔·里斯 (Angel Reese) 对两队之间的一场比赛结果下注 400 美元，“没有兑现目标”。
一位直接了解此事的人士告诉美联社，球员不会因为这次赌注而受到惩罚。由于情况敏感，该人士不愿透露姓名。
联盟发布了全明星周末的最初视频，就在布克斯的达拉斯翼队和里斯的亚特兰大梦队定于周三晚上比赛的几天前。在这段视频中，布克斯和里斯对比赛下了看似个人的赌注。它的标题是“我们做到了？”后面是一个大笑的表情符号，“佩奇·布克斯在全明星周末与安吉尔·里斯打赌今晚的比赛。”
WNBA 迅速采取行动删除了这条消息，但在该消息被分享到社交媒体之前。
联盟发言人周四表示：“虽然社交媒体帖子的目的是轻松愉快，但 WNBA 球员很清楚联盟禁止投注 WNBA 比赛的政策，并且每年都会接受培训以强化这些政策。”“我们认识到这篇文章没有切中要害，在发布后不久就将其删除，并在内部解决了这个问题。
“我们还将以此为契机，向相关球员再次强调，有关 WNBA 比赛投注的对话，即使是开玩笑，也可能会产生负面后果。”
当被要求置评时，飞翼队和梦想队都尊重联盟的声明。
联盟的集体谈判协议规定，严格禁止任何形式的投注，并且由专员自行决定对球员处以罚款、停赛甚至取消 WNBA 资格。
周三，梦想队在落后 15 分的情况下奋起反击，以 82-81 击败了 Wings，里斯得到 22 分和 12 个篮板，布克斯得到 16 分和 6 次助攻。

item.title: 唱片学院首席执行官回应 BTS 不提交格莱美奖的决定
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——唱片学院首席执行官小哈维·梅森 (Harvey Mason jr.)回应了韩国流行音乐巨头 BTS 将不会在即将举行的 2027 年格莱美颁奖典礼上提交他们的音乐以供考虑的消息。
“我很遗憾听到 BTS 选择不参加今年的格莱美颁奖典礼，但作为音乐创作者，我理解并尊重他们的决定，”小梅森说道。在格莱美奖官方 Instagram 页面上写道。
周三，所有七名 BTS 成员——RM、Suga、j-hope、Jimin、V、Jung Kook 和 Jin——在 Instagram 上分享了同一条信息，表示他们不会向格莱美奖提交他们的复出专辑《ARIRANG》或其歌曲。
他们写道：“我们希望我们的音乐能够因其本来面目而被听到和喜爱，而不是被地区或语言所划分。”就在一个月后，唱片学院宣布了五个新的格莱美类别，其中包括最佳亚洲流行音乐表演。
2026 年 7 月 19 日，防弹少年团在纽约附近的新泽西州东卢瑟福举行的世界杯决赛西班牙队与阿根廷队之间的中场表演。（美联社照片/Matt Rourke，档案）
根据规则手册，该类别认可韩国流行音乐、日本流行音乐、中国流行音乐等领域的发行作品。但一些粉丝认为这是亚洲表演者的种族障碍。
小梅森在声明中。表示，创建新类别是为了庆祝亚洲音乐界更多的声音，而不是将这些艺术家与其他奖项分开。
“我确实想澄清一些在谈话中似乎被忽视的事情。亚洲流行类别的创建是为了庆祝来自亚洲的流行艺术的深度、多样性和非凡的发展，”他写道。“更多类别意味着更多艺术家的作品得到认可。这绝不是为了划分，而是为了扩大我们 15,000 名格莱美选民的认可范围。”
他补充说，提交流派类别（例如新亚洲流行奖）并不排除艺术家提交年度专辑、歌曲和唱片等一般领域类别。
“流派类别中的认可和一般领域中的认可并不相互排斥，”小梅森说。说。“艺术家绝对可以两者兼而有之。”
录音学院首席执行官小哈维·梅森 (Harvey Mason Jr.) 在 2026 年 2 月 1 日于洛杉矶举行的第 68 届格莱美颁奖典礼上发表讲话。（美联社照片/克里斯·皮泽罗，档案）
BTS 从未赢得过格莱美奖，尽管他们已获得五次提名：三次获得最佳流行二人组/团体表演奖提名，并获得年度专辑奖（因其对酷玩乐队“Music of the Spheres”的贡献）以及“Yet to Come”的最佳音乐录影带奖。
事实上，在今年之前，还没有韩国流行音乐艺人赢得过格莱美奖，当时 Netflix 动画电影《KPop Demon Hunters》中的《Golden》夺得了视觉媒体最佳歌曲奖杯。它为韩国流行音乐在格莱美颁奖典礼上的一个引人注目的夜晚画上了圆满的句号——尽管该流派在格莱美颁奖典礼上拥有大量的国际追随者，但长期以来却没有得到足够的重视。

item.title: 美国第二季度经济增长低迷1.5%，通胀居高不下
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——由于进口增加拖累经济增长，美国经济从 4 月到 6 月缓慢增长 1.5%，但消费者仍在继续消费。美联储青睐的通胀指标上个月增长更为缓慢。但在距离中期选举还有不到 100 天的时间，美国人对高生活成本感到沮丧之际，该利率仍高于央行 2% 的目标。
美国商务部周四报告称，2026 年前三个月美国国内生产总值（即美国商品和服务产出）增速从 2.1% 放缓，低于经济学家的预期。但占美国经济活动约 70% 的消费者支出年增长率为 3.2%，高于 1 月至 3 月期间的 0.5%。
衡量经济潜在实力的指标 — — 排除不稳定的政府支出和贸易数据 — — 看起来不错，年增长率为 3.9%，高于 1 月至 3 月的 1.7%。
2026 年 7 月 6 日星期一，伊利诺伊州阿灵顿高地的一家杂货店，一名员工在收银台检查酒品前检查顾客的身份证。（美联社照片/Nam Y. Huh）
不包括住房在内的商业投资增长 8.4%，低于 1 月至 3 月的 10.6%，但强劲，反映出人工智能投资的激增。
经济数据中减去了进口，因为 GDP 只应该计算美国的生产量。进口增长 11.5%，部分原因是计算机芯片和其他支持人工智能投资的产品出货量激增。进口使第二季度 GDP 增长下降 1.5%。
惠誉评级美国经济主管奥卢·索诺拉表示：“消费者拯救了这个季度。人工智能投资仍然是一个强劲的增长故事，但支撑这一增长的进口激增提醒人们，人工智能的繁荣并不会自动转化为对美国 GDP 的同样巨大的推动。”
美国商务部周四还表示，美联储青睐的个人消费支出（PCE）价格指数上个月自 2025 年 6 月起上涨 3.7%，低于 5 月份的同比涨幅 4.1%。剔除波动较大的食品和能源价格，所谓的核心消费者价格同比上涨3.3%，与5月份3.4%的涨幅相比变化不大。由于汽油和其他能源产品价格下降 9.2%，5 月至 6 月价格实际上下降了 0.1%。
2026 年 7 月 23 日星期四，科罗拉多州戈尔登，70 号州际公路沿线的辛克莱加油站显示汽油价格。（美联社照片/David Zalubowski）
PCE价格大致符合经济学家的预期。但五年多来，物价同比涨幅一直高于美联储 2% 的目标，一些美联储官员对遏制通胀的进展感到不耐烦。
美联储周三选择连续第五次会议维持基准利率不变。但三位地区联储主席持不同意见，称他们希望加息以应对通胀上升。
面对伊朗战争及其造成的能源价格飙升，美国经济表现出惊人的弹性。今年就业市场已从 2025 年的低迷状态中反弹，为消费者提供了必要的消费资金。今年，雇主平均每月增加 92,000 个工作岗位，而 2025 年，高利率和唐纳德·特朗普总统不稳定的关税使用阻碍了企业招聘，每月增加的工作岗位不到 10,000 个。
在 11 月中期选举之前，高昂的成本让美国人感到沮丧，这将决定唐纳德·特朗普总统的共和党是否能完全控制国会
美联社-NORC 的一项新民意调查发现，公众对伊朗战争感到不满。大约十分之七的美国成年人（72%）表示，阻止国内石油和天然气价格上涨对美国来说“极其”或“非常”重要，这一比例高于 3 月份的 67%。

item.title: 在价格和引起腹泻的寄生虫之间，生菜给一些餐馆带来了困难
item.description:
It’s been a choppy year for restaurants that lean into lettuce.
Lettuce prices rose sharply in the first half of 2026 due to hot weather in Arizona, where about one-third of America’s lettuce is grown. Now, restaurants are dealing with the fallout from acyclospora outbreaklinked to shredded lettuce that has sickened thousands of Americans.
Yum Brands, the parent company ofTaco Bell, said Thursday that Taco Bell’s U.S. same-store sales are down 2% so far in the July-September period due to customers’ concerns over the outbreak. That compares to a 7% same-store sales increase in the April-June period.
Federal health officials first tied the diarrhea-causing outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell restaurants in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia. Later, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration said customers in Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma and Pennsylvania werealso affected.
Taco Bell removed shredded iceberg lettuce supplied byTaylor Farmsfrom its U.S. restaurants on July 17. The following day,Taylor Farmsrecalled iceberg lettuce grown in central Mexico.
Taco Bell’s sales bottomed out the weekend of July 18-19 but have been steadily improving since then, Yum Brands Chief Financial Officer Ranjith Roy said Thursday in a conference call with investors. Over the last four days, Taco Bell’s U.S. sales have climbed halfway back to their year-ago level, he said.
Yum Brands CEO Chris Turner said Taco Bell’s quick action to contain the issue and its clear communication on social media helped bring diners back. The brand also enticed fans with daily specials like $1 Mexican pizza.
“With respect to the consumer sentiment, we’ve seen real improvement as consumers have understood better the nature of the issue,” Turner said. “They understand that it is not a Taco Bell specific issue.”
Other chains are also feeling some impact from the outbreak even though they haven’t been named in government investigations. Chipotle Mexican Grill said Wednesday that it expects its same-store sales to rise only 1% in the July-September period because of lower traffic due to the outbreak. It had previously expected same-store sales to rise 3% in that period.
Foot traffic at Chopt, a salad-focused chain with 105 locations, plunged 24% on July 18 compared to the normal average for a Saturday, according to Placer.ai, a market research company. M Science, another market research firm, found that weekly spending at the salad chain Sweetgreen dropped 10 percentage points compared to last year during the first half of July.
Chopt didn’t respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press. Sweetgreen, which has 285 U.S. locations, did not confirm a drop in sales and said in a statement that its food hasn’t been connected to the current cyclospora outbreak.
“We follow rigorous food safety standards and can trace our ingredients from restaurant to farm,” the company said.
Cyclospora cases have continued to grow. As of July 27, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said it has received reports of 6,707 laboratory-confirmed cases. It’s investigating multiple clusters, including anew outbreakinvolving 72 people that was announced last week. As theFDA investigationprogresses, officials should get a better understanding of which illnesses are connected and “how complex this outbreak actually has become,” said Craig Hedberg, a food safety researcher at the University of Minnesota.
The outbreak came on top of an already difficult year for the lettuce industry and people who love eating salads. The retail price of a pound of iceberg lettuce jumped nearly 20% between January and June of this year, according to government data. Consumers paid an average of 33% more last month for all fresh lettuce compared to a year earlier, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said.
Lettuce prices advertised by major grocery stores last week averaged $1.86 for a head of iceberg, 25 cents more than the same week a year earlier, according to the USDA. A head of red leaf lettuce cost 52 cents more at $1.66, and a bunch of romaine had an advertised price of $2.49, which was $1.55 higher, the department reported.
Shoppers caught a break with some types of salad mixes, though, which stores advertised at prices 7 to 24 cents cheaper than a year prior, the USDA said.
Elizabeth Canales, an associate professor of agricultural economics at Mississippi State University, said unusually hot weather in Arizona early in the year caused crops to mature too early. That caused big supply gaps until California production began in late April.
Fuel costs, which increased after the U.S. and Israel launched strikeson Iranand Iran blocked most oil tankers from leaving the Persian Gulf, have also been an issue, according to Canales. Lettuce is especially perishable and requires energy for cooling from the time it’s picked to the time it’s sold, Canales said.
“The cold chain needs to be maintained. Cooling and transporting it is very important,” Canales said.
Lettuce has been linked to multiple food poisoning outbreaks in the past, including two in 2018 involving E. coli linked to romaine lettuce grownin ArizonaandCalifornia.
Associated Press Writer Mike Stobbe contributed from New York.

item.title: 美国30年期平均抵押贷款利率升至一年来最高水平6.66%
item.description:
美国平均长期抵押贷款利率连续第四周上升至一年来的最高水平，这对希望摆脱住房贷款借贷成本上升的潜在购房者来说又是一次挫折。
抵押贷款买家房地美 (Freddie Mac) 周四表示，基准 30 年期固定利率抵押贷款利率从上周的 6.58% 升至 6.66%。一年前，平均利率为6.72%。
较高的抵押贷款利率可能会增加借款人每月数百美元的成本，从而限制购房者的购买力。随着利率上升，可能会导致潜在购房者推迟购房，这也是今年美国房屋销售低迷的原因之一。
为住房贷款再融资的借款人经常寻求的 15 年期固定利率抵押贷款的借贷成本本周也有所上升。该平均利率从上周的 5.96% 上升至 6.04%。房地美表示，一年前该利率为 5.85%。
抵押贷款利率受到多种因素的影响，从美联储的利率政策决策到债券市场投资者对经济和通胀的预期。它们通常遵循 10 年期国债收益率的轨迹，贷方将其用作住房贷款定价的指南。
由于伊朗战争导致原油价格大幅上涨，加剧了通胀加剧的预期，今年利率大多上涨。这推高了长期债券收益率（相对于二月底冲突开始前的水平），导致抵押贷款利率走高。
截至周四中午，债券市场10年期国债收益率为4.66%。战争爆发前的 2 月底，这一数字仅为 3.97%。
30年期抵押贷款的平均利率目前为2025年7月31日以来的最高水平，当时为6.72%。就在 2 月底，平均利率自 2022 年底以来首次跌破 6%。
最新一次抵押贷款利率上调是在美联储维持关键利率不变的第二天，美联储正在努力应对如何抑制顽固的高通胀，五年多来通胀率一直高于央行 2% 的目标。
在本周央行为期两天的货币政策会议上，三位地区联储行长反对提高利率以应对高物价。
Realtor.com 高级经济学家安东尼·史密斯表示，这表明美联储成员不再在通胀问题上步调一致，他们的下一步行动也不会是降息。
史密斯表示：“由于美联储暗示下一步行动更有可能是加息而不是降息，短期内降息的可能性似乎不大。”“由于石油仍然是伊朗冲突助长通胀的主要渠道，因此局势缓和和霍尔木兹海峡的重新开放仍然是回归较低利率的最明确路径。”
央行不设定抵押贷款利率，但其提高或降低短期利率的决定受到债券投资者的密切关注，并最终可能影响十年期国债的收益率。
尽管平均长期抵押贷款利率仍低于去年同期，但其上升趋势拖累了今年的房屋销售。经季节性调整后，1 月至 6 月美国二手房销量与去年同期相比增长了 0.7%，但仍徘徊在每年 400 万套附近，远低于接近 520 万套的历史正常水平。
这一趋势延续了自 2022 年开始的全国房地产市场低迷，当时抵押贷款利率开始从大流行时代的低点攀升。去年美国二手房销售量基本持平，处于 30 年来的最低水平。
抵押贷款申请的最新数据显示，抵押贷款利率的上升趋势让一些潜在购房者有理由停下来。
根据抵押贷款银行家协会的数据，上周抵押贷款申请（包括购房贷款或现有抵押贷款再融资）比前一周下降了 6.4%。
MBA 首席执行官 Bob Broeksmit 表示：“虽然即将公布的经济数据将继续影响利率前景，但借贷成本上升对于许多潜在购房者来说仍然是今年夏天的一个挑战。”
